title: Lullabies she sang to her children
summary: She says she sang to put her sons to sleep, cannot recall the songs, and the interviewer offers to bring tapes next time.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: What kind of Mardi Gras song? That's a Mardi Gras song. That's a what kind of Mardi Gras song? That's a Mardi Gras song. Did you ever try to play those songs your mother was singing on your clarinet when you were younger? No, no, no. What? I wondered if George ever tried to play any of those songs when he'd hear you sing them, and you picked up your clarinet if you used to practice on them.
No, because you see, I would sing when I was putting him and my other son, Sidney, and them, but they were babies almost.
What sort of songs did you used to sing when you were putting them to sleep?
Oh, anything would come to my mind.
Do you remember the names of some of the songs or a little bit of some of them?
I remember Le Dr. Noir I used to sing and Fais du Dau.

Tous les jours dimanche, tous les jours c'est fait, tous les jours tombeau dans car à nous, ça n'a fait pour ça. Can you sing? Can you sing a little of that? Yeah, I used to sing that for them, yes. Sing a little bit of it now, if you will. Well, I just sang tous les jours c'est fait, tous les jours dimanche.
You spoke it, you didn't sing it, you spoke it.
I did sing it. Oh, yes. And I just cannot remember, and gracious knows I used to sing, sing, sing to my children to put them to sleep.

I have, uh, some recordings of, uh, or a couple of people who are in the same general background, you are, and, uh, next time I come, I'd like to play you some, uh, tapes of some, uh, French singers. They're younger than you are, but they know some of the same songs.
They'll probably refresh your memory, and you'll probably remember some things.
You see, of course, now, I forget, I'm old.
